what_happened: Job 20261029-212839-tcjb ("Refuse readings that defer a numbered request part or Acceptance bullet", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. The critic said the reading misread the request, and after the last round (5) the plan still needed revising. The reading's criterion 4 defined the "standard Steward bullets" from memory. The bullets Steward really generates (steward.rs:620-624) are different, and the long-title "The change is made as described: <title>" bullet was left out. The plan's demonstration for criterion 4 used invented bullet text. Under the ceil(n/2) stem threshold, the real standard bullet would be refused, and the job's own request and reading would probably be refused too. Two major findings: (1) the coverage threshold refuses the real standard Steward bullet and the criterion-4 demo does not test it; (2) the request-wide split exemption fires on common words such as "split" and "separately", so ordinary requests could switch the check off. Four minor findings: the 5% refusal estimate has no basis, numbered lines copied by generators are not parts, "distinctive stem" is undefined, and fake.rs is not in the deliverables. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named files and functions exist, but nothing makes the reading or plan run a new matching rule against the real shapes it must accept. Here those are the bullets steward.rs generates and the Acceptance lists in past requests. The reading wrote the standard bullets from memory, and the plan's fixtures copied that text. The coverage threshold and the split-exemption word list were therefore never tried on real text. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step, so two major findings that survive round 5 lose all planning spend.
other_causes: The plan has no corpus replay of its own: the 5% refusal estimate is stated without a basis, and the real replay runs only at verification.
The reading was accepted without cross-checking its quoted bullet text against steward.rs, which the request itself named.
Terms such as "distinctive stem" and the split-exemption trigger words were left undefined, so the plan's rule could not be tested.
open_hypotheses: The input does not show whether the critic's round-1 finding on the standard bullets was fed back to the planner in later rounds and ignored, or whether the planner could not fix it.
The input does not show whether the critic's hand count that this job's own request would be refused is accurate.
contradictions: The critic confirmed the plan's structure, named files, functions and line anchors exist, so the plan was mostly sound. Only the matching rules and fixtures failed.
prevention: Before a reading or plan for a new matching or refusal rule is accepted, Athena should run the draft matcher over the real input shapes. These are the bullets steward.rs generates, including the long-title "as described" case, and the Acceptance lists in recorded past requests. The expected refusal share should be measured from that run, not estimated. Fixtures should be taken from those recorded shapes, and any exemption word list should be checked against the same corpus. The planning stage should keep the best plan across rounds and run a mechanical repair round for gaps that the code answers.
proposed_request: Refuse readings that defer a numbered request part or an Acceptance bullet, in one job, with these outcomes. (1) The refusal check in checks.rs refuses a reading when a numbered part of the request, or an Acceptance bullet, is deferred or dropped, and does not refuse readings that cover them. (2) A criterion may cover a standard Steward bullet. The standard bullets are the ones steward.rs generates (lines 620-624): "The change is made as described: <title>", "No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass" and "fmt, clippy and test pass". The long-title "as described" bullet must be accepted. (3) The split exemption fires only on an explicit instruction to split the request into separate jobs, not on common words such as "split" or "separately". (4) Define "distinctive stem" in the code comment. (5) Tests take their fixtures from real Steward output and from recorded past requests, and include this request and its accepted reading, which must not be refused. (6) The replay over past requests reports the real refusal share, and the doc comment states that measured figure. (7) fmt, clippy and test pass, and the CHANGELOG.md has an entry. Add crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs to the deliverables if the tests need it.
